I spent three months building a full-stack MERN project for the college hackathon, but I withdrew our team's submission at 4 AM last night because the UI didn't look as slick as the seniors' projects. I’d rather they hate me for quitting than find out I'm actually incompetent.

I cleared four rounds of interviews for a product company, but in the final HR round, I stuttered while explaining my minor project architecture. I can't stop replaying those 10 seconds of silence in my head, feeling absolutely nauseous, and I didn't even go for the pool campus drive today because what's the point? If I messed up a basic HR round when the finish line was right there, I'm clearly not cut out for this industry.

I received a 75% on my midterms instead of my usual 90%+, and now I can't even open my books to study for the upcoming end-sems. I'm literally self-sabotaging my entire semester because if I can't guarantee an A grade, my brain refuses to let me even try.

I got a 9.4 CGPA but I didn't clear the LeetCode medium round for the Amazon intern shortlist today. Everyone in my hostel wing is celebrating because they got in with 8.2s and 8.5s, and I'm just sitting here in the dark locking my door. I feel like a total fraud, like my entire academic life has been a waste because when it actually mattered, I choked. If I can't even solve a basic tree problem under pressure, I'm never going to get placed.

I’ve spent the last six hours trying to debug this graph representation for my lab submission tomorrow and I’m literally shaking. I want to ask the TA or post on the class Discord, but I'm terrified they’ll realize I don’t belong in this branch. I’ve always been the 'smart one' in my family, but now I’m just staring at a segmentation fault, crying silently so my roommate doesn’t hear me. If I can't do this on my own, I don't deserve to be here.

My dad just called to tell me our neighbor’s son got a 45 LPA off-campus placement at Adobe. I scored a 9.1 last semester and got an offer for 12 LPA, but when I told him, he just asked why I didn't try for the higher bracket. I feel sick to my stomach, like my hard work is completely invisible because it's not the absolute best. Why does every achievement feel like a failure the moment someone else does slightly better?

I haven't opened my compiler design notes in three days even though the midterms start on Monday. Every time I try to study, my mind just goes entirely blank because I know if I don't get an S-grade, my CGPA will drop below 9.0 and I'll lose my scholarship. I’m so paralyzed by the fear of failing that I’m literally sabotaging myself by sleeping 14 hours a day to escape the anxiety. I hate myself for being this weak.

I'm doing 90% of the work for our final year capstone project because my teammates keep writing messy, unoptimized code. They think I'm being a control freak, but if our system latency goes up during the external evaluation, the external examiner will tank our grades. Everyone in my wing is blasting music and celebrating their offers, and I'm literally sitting in the dark of the common washroom crying because if I'm not the top select, I'm just a useless failure who lucked out until now. I saw my Operating Systems midterm paper and I got an 8 out of 10 while the class average was 6. I’ve blocked my classmates on WhatsApp because I can't stand them asking 'how much did you get' and then acting like I'm humblebragging when I'm genuinely physically sick to my stomach over my own stupidity.

The external examiner smirked during my compiler design viva when I got confused between LL and LR parsers, and I just froze. I came back to my hostel room, locked the door, and I've been staring at my DBMS textbook for five hours without reading a single line because what's the point of studying if I'm just going to choke under pressure again? I can still hear his stupid laugh and it feels like my entire academic identity just shattered over one wrong answer.

My cousin just bagged a 28 LPA SDE role at Amazon, and at dinner, my mom casually mentioned how 'some people just know how to crack the system on the first try.' I have a 14 LPA offer which I worked my absolute ass off for, but now I feel like an absolute embarrassment to this family. I spent the whole night deleting my resume drafts and GitHub repos because if I can't be the best child, I don't even want to pretend I'm trying anymore.

Our Web Dev project submission deadline was 11:59 PM, and the code was 95% functional, but the UI alignment on mobile devices was slightly off. I couldn't bring myself to upload something so messy, so I kept tweaking the CSS until 12:05 AM and ended up missing the portal entirely, getting a zero for the milestone. My team members are furious and I'm just sitting here wanting to disappear because my obsession with making it perfect completely ruined it for everyone.

I spent three weeks formatting my final year thesis, and when my professor pointed out a tiny formatting error, my chest tightened. I wanted to tear up the whole project. If it's not perfect, what's the point?
I can't accept anything less than I feel like a fraud who just got lucky. I'm exhausting myself and my sleep is ruined.
